title: Triangle Type
problem: Read three positive integers on one line: the lengths of three sides. If the two shorter sides together are not longer than the longest side, they cannot form a triangle, so print Not a triangle. Otherwise print Equilateral if all three sides are equal, Isosceles if exactly two are equal, and Scalene if all three are different. For example, 3 4 5 gives Scalene and 5 5 8 gives Isosceles.
starter_code:
# Read three side lengths on one line.
# Print Not a triangle, Equilateral, Isosceles or Scalene.

# Write your code here

hints.1: Decide whether the sides can form a triangle at all before you look at how many of them are equal.
hints.2: Sort the three sides so the longest is last. If the two shorter ones do not add up to more than the longest, it is not a triangle. Otherwise count how many sides are equal.

failure_explanation: Check that a triangle is possible first: two shorter sides that add up to exactly the longest side still do not make one, and a set of sides with two equal lengths can still be impossible. The sides can come in any order, so compare every pair and not only the first two.
